newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan seeks adviser on sale of investment unit.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan seeks adviser on sale of investment unit.

text.p: Pakistan's Privatisation Commission said it was seeking a financial adviser for the privatisation of the Investment Corporation of Pakistan (ICP).
It said in a statement received on Thursday that interested parties should submit expressions of interest to the commission by June 23.
ICP began operations in February 1996 with a brief to broaden the base of investments and develop the capital market in Pakistan, the statement said.
It was mandated to underwrite share issues, participate in equity projects, open investment accounts and term deposit accounts, and float and manage closed-end mutual funds.
The statement said ICP had earned "reasonably good profits", declaring dividends on its mutual funds. It gave no details.
Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif's government, which took power in February, has pledged to speed up the privatisation of state utilities, banks, financial institutions and industrial units.
